claim.pdf_says: 8.9 Reserved words — page 235 column 3 ends with 'END-PERFORM' as its last entry. 'END-RECEIVE', 'END-READ', 'END-RETURN', 'END-REWRITE', 'END-SEARCH' are the first five entries of column 1 on the NEXT page (PDF p236, printed page 206), each on its own line (verified by rendering p236).
claim.markdown_says: specs/ISO_COBOL.md:10325 — 'END-PERFORM END-RECEIVE END-READ END-RETURN END-REWRITE END-SEARCH' (six reserved words on a single line, immediately before the anchor). Every other entry in 8.9 is one word per line.
claim.why_it_matters: Clause 8.9 is a machine-readable list and this project consumes it directly to build the reserved-word table. Five of the six words on this line are no longer separate list entries, so any line-oriented extraction of 8.9 drops END-RECEIVE, END-READ, END-RETURN, END-REWRITE and END-SEARCH, and additionally mis-attributes them to page 235 instead of page 236.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed on both sides; every element of the claim checks out. PDF side. Rendered p235 at 300dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v235/spec_p235.png, printed page 205). Clause 8.9 'Reserved words' opens on this page with a three-column list. Column 3 runs ... END-IF, END-MULTIPLY, END-OF-PAGE, END-PERFORM and STOPS there — END-PERFORM is unambiguously the last printed entry on the page; the remaining ~15% of the text block is blank before the '©ISO/IEC 2023 205' footer. No trace of END-RECEIVE/END-READ/END-RETURN/END-REWRITE/END-SEARCH anywhere on p235. Also rendered p236 (printed page 206) to see where those words actually live. Column 1 begins exactly: END-RECEIVE / END-READ / END-RETURN / END-REWRITE / END-SEARCH / END-SEND / EMD-START / END-STRING / ... — five separate entries on five separate lines, in that order. Note ISO's own non-alphabetical ordering (END-RECEIVE printed before END-READ) and ISO's own typo 'EMD-START'; the markdown faithfully reproduces both, which shows the transcription did not lose or reorder words — the defect is purely the line join. Markdown side. specs/ISO_COBOL.md:10325 is literally 'END-PERFORM END-RECEIVE END-READ END-RETURN END-REWRITE END-SEARCH' (verified with sed and cat -A: one line, single spaces, no trailing markers). Line 10326 is blank and line 10327 is '', so all six words sit inside the page-235 span. The markdown's page-236 section starts at END-SEND — so the five words exist NOWHERE ELSE in 8.9: grep over the whole file shows END-REWRITE and END-SEARCH occur in clause 8.9 only on line 10325 (all other hits are the REWRITE/SEARCH general formats around lines 30096/30427/30454, statement-scope tables at 23595/23597, code examples, and index entries). The one-word-per-line invariant is real, not an assumption: scanning the 8.9 block for any line matching two adjacent uppercase tokens returns exactly three hits plus the closing NOTE — i.e. ~1000 entries are one word per line and only the page-boundary lines are joined. This is not page-break furniture, wrapping, or hyphenation. Real hyphenated continuations in this list ARE handled correctly and look completely different (p236 prints 'FLOAT-NOT-A-NUMBER-' / ' QUIET' as a wrapped single entry). Here six independent list entries were concatenated into one line and five of them were pulled backwards across a page boundary, so meaning IS changed for the consuming use: a line-oriented reader of 8.9 sees 1 malformed entry where the standard prints 6. Severity 'structural' is right — 8.9 is the normative source for the reserved-word table (4.2.8 requires an implementation to recognize all of them), so a dropped word is a compiler that accepts a reserved word as a user-defined name.
verdict.corrected_description: The claim is accurate as written. Two sharpenings for the fix. (1) Six entries are damaged, not five. END-PERFORM is also no longer a standalone entry — a line-oriented extractor of 8.9 does not emit END-PERFORM plus five drops, it emits ONE bogus 6-word 'reserved word' and zero of the six correct entries. The repair is to split line 10325 into 'END-PERFORM' on p235 and END-RECEIVE / END-READ / END-RETURN / END-REWRITE / END-SEARCH as five lines placed AFTER the anchor (line 10327), ahead of the existing END-SEND, preserving ISO's printed order (END-RECEIVE before END-READ). (2) It is a PATTERN, not a one-off — every 8.9 page boundary has the same run-on defect, so fix all three in one change set: • line 10325 (p235→p236): 'END-PERFORM' | END-RECEIVE END-READ END-RETURN END-REWRITE END-SEARCH — END-PERFORM is p235 col 3's last entry; the five belong to p236 col 1 (confirmed against both renders). • line 10466 (p236→p237): 'NUMERIC-EDITED OBJECT OBJECT-COMPUTER OBJECT-REFERENCE OCCURS OF' — the p236 render confirms NUMERIC-EDITED is that page's last col-3 entry, so OBJECT, OBJECT-COMPUTER, OBJECT-REFERENCE, OCCURS and OF belong to p237. • line 10584 (p237→p238): 'SYSTEM-DEFAULT TABLE TALLYING TERMINATE TEST THAN' — same shape; TABLE, TALLYING, TERMINATE, TEST and THAN belong to p238 (worth re-rendering p237/p238 to confirm the split point before editing). Across the three boundaries 15 reserved words are mis-attributed and 18 entries are unextractable. Unrelated but adjacent: 'EMD-START' at p236 col 1 is ISO's OWN printed typo for END-START and the markdown reproduces it correctly — do not 'fix' it in the transcription; record it as an ISO defect and normalize it in the reserved-word table build instead.
